Method of Attack: Covert channels exploiting software-based network isolation flaws in routers
Direct covert channels via specially-crafted network packets (DHCP, IGMP, ARP) that bypass network segmentation
Timing-based covert channels using shared hardware resources (CPU time, network and memory buffers) to encode data
Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) to increase CPU load for timing channel
Exploitation of DHCP NAK broadcast to both guest and host networks
Use of IGMP membership queries and ARP broadcast packets to smuggle data
Use of SSH aborted key exchange to create CPU load timing channel
Use of ping and ICMP packets to influence router response times
Discoverer: Researchers at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev
Impacted Systems: Routers from TP-Link (Archer C3200, Archer C2)
Attack Vector: Exploitation of software-based network isolation in routers
Sending specially-crafted network packets (DHCP, IGMP, ARP) that are erroneously forwarded to both guest and host networks
Timing-based covert channels via shared hardware resource usage
Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) via exposed web management interface
